resource.name: John Fisher Free Legal Advice Clinic
resource.description: Initial advice on consumer, employment, family, housing and insurance problems.
resource.who: People who live or work in Brent.
resource.access: Use the clinic contact details on the LawWorks page to ask about an appointment. Do not attend without confirmation.
resource.check: Free initial legal advice. Confirm the session and any assessment requirements before attending.
resource.coverage: Brent residents and people working in Brent.

sources.note: LawWorks lists this specific clinic, its legal topics, Brent eligibility and appointment-only access. A current Citizens Advice Brent partner search result also describes its free Tuesday-evening service.

candidates.evidence: LawWorks lists this specific clinic, its legal topics, Brent eligibility and appointment-only access. A current Citizens Advice Brent partner search result also describes its free Tuesday-evening service.
candidates.limitations: Current appointment availability was not confirmed. The provider legal-advice URL did not load; the listing uses the readable official clinic-network page and does not reproduce its telephone number.

resource.name: Sangam Advice Centre — legal advice
resource.description: Advice on welfare, housing, immigration, employment, debt and family matters.
resource.who: Adults over 18 who live, work or study in Barnet, Brent or Harrow.
resource.access: Phone 020 8952 7062 to ask about the advice you need and how to access it.
resource.check: The NHS profile lists legal advice as free. Confirm current arrangements and whether the service can help with your issue.
resource.coverage: Barnet, Brent and Harrow; this listing provides the Harrow access route.

sources.note: The NHS profile describes free legal advice for adults over 18 living, working or studying in Barnet, Brent or Harrow, with a service contact number.

candidates.evidence: The NHS profile describes free legal advice for adults over 18 living, working or studying in Barnet, Brent or Harrow, with a service contact number.
candidates.limitations: NHS record supplied on 18 August 2026. Current waiting times, appointment arrangements and accessibility were not confirmed. No duplicate local entries were created for other areas.

resource.name: FirmFoundation — Harrow food and shower drop-in
resource.description: A local drop-in offering food, showers and contact with homelessness support.
resource.who: People with no accommodation who are sleeping rough in Harrow.
resource.access: Use the provider contact page or phone 020 8426 5515 to check visiting arrangements at the Welldon Centre, Welldon Crescent, Harrow HA1 1QR.
resource.check: Confirm current opening times and any charges before travelling. This is a drop-in support route, not a promise of a shelter bed.

sources.note: The provider access page identifies rough sleepers in Harrow and its food/shower drop-in. Its contact page gives the Welldon Centre location, office contact and regular drop-in sessions.
Provider contact page read: drop-in location, regular sessions and office contact published.

candidates.evidence: The provider access page identifies rough sleepers in Harrow and its food/shower drop-in. Its contact page gives the Welldon Centre location, office contact and regular drop-in sessions.
candidates.limitations: Costs and current capacity are not stated. Accommodation eligibility and bed availability were not assessed.

resource.name: Nucleus Legal Advice Centre — Kensington and Chelsea
resource.description: Advice on welfare benefits, housing, debt and money, employment and other legal issues, with enquiry routes for local residents.
resource.who: People living in Kensington and Chelsea who need advice on employment, debt, housing, immigration or general legal issues.
resource.access: Use the relevant enquiry form on the provider page or call 020 7373 4005. The centre is at 298 Old Brompton Road, SW5 9JF.
resource.check: Contact Nucleus first to confirm which adviser, appointment or drop-in route fits your issue.

sources.note: Current provider page names its Kensington and Chelsea work, advice areas, enquiry forms, phone number and local address.
Current NHS profile confirms the local population, advice subjects, address, phone and provider website; information supplied 11 September 2026.

candidates.evidence: The provider offers welfare-benefit, housing, debt and money and pro-bono solicitor routes from its Kensington and Chelsea page; the NHS profile independently states that it advises borough residents on employment, debt, housing, immigration and general legal issues.
candidates.limitations: Eligibility, adviser capacity, appointment availability, accessibility and any charges for particular casework were not established; contact the service before attending.

resource.name: KCSC Directory of Local Organisations
resource.description: Search voluntary and community organisations operating in Kensington and Chelsea by name, beneficiary group or activity type.
resource.who: People looking for local voluntary and community organisations and the services or activities they provide in Kensington and Chelsea.
resource.access: Search by name or use the beneficiary-group and activity-type filters, then contact the relevant organisation directly.
resource.check: KCSC says organisations supply their own details and changes may not always be reported, so confirm current information with the organisation.
resource.coverage: Voluntary organisations operating in Kensington and Chelsea

sources.note: The current KCSC page identifies a directory of organisations operating in the borough, explains its search filters and warns users to confirm details with providers.

candidates.evidence: Kensington & Chelsea Social Council publishes a live directory with name, beneficiary and activity filters and populated organisation records for voluntary organisations operating in the borough.
candidates.limitations: The directory is informational rather than an endorsement; entries are supplied by organisations and KCSC says it may not always be told about changes.

resource.name: South Westminster Legal Advice Centre
resource.description: Volunteer lawyers provide legal advice for people on low incomes, including help understanding rights in disputes and non-contentious matters.
resource.who: Primarily people who live or work in Westminster and cannot afford a solicitor, including homeless people with a Westminster connection.
resource.access: Book an appointment through the provider website. The service does not currently accept drop-ins.
resource.check: Advice is free, but the centre requests small donations for some letters, documents and photocopies; check whether it can advise on your issue before booking.
resource.coverage: City of Westminster, with surrounding postcodes considered when resources permit

sources.note: The provider states its Westminster connection and low-income criteria, advice-only scope, free advice and small requested document or copying donations.
The current home page confirms appointment-only access, the inability to accept drop-ins, free advice and service for people living or working in or near Westminster.

candidates.evidence: The provider's current pages say volunteer lawyers give free advice to people who cannot afford legal help, primarily those living or working in Westminster, and require users to make an appointment online.
candidates.limitations: The centre gives advice rather than legal representation and depends on volunteer capacity. It requests small donations for certain written work or copies, and help outside Westminster is only offered when resources permit.

resource.name: ASSIST — adult autism support in Westminster
resource.description: One-to-one practical support and social groups for autistic adults or adults actively seeking an autism diagnosis.
resource.who: Westminster residents aged 18 or over who have or are seeking an autism diagnosis and are not eligible for adult social care support.
resource.access: Contact ASSIST for an appointment by emailing assistlondon@nas.org.uk or calling 020 8962 3015.
resource.check: Ask ASSIST to confirm that you meet its current criteria and which appointment or group is suitable.

sources.note: The Westminster council page, updated 15 January 2026, gives the service activity, eligibility, appointment route, opening times and contact details.

candidates.evidence: Westminster City Council says ASSIST provides one-to-one appointments and social groups, gives explicit adult autism and adult-social-care eligibility criteria, and publishes direct email and phone access routes.
candidates.limitations: The page's overview also mentions Hammersmith and Fulham, while its detailed access criteria name Westminster or Kensington and Chelsea; this proposal is limited to the unambiguous Westminster coverage. Current capacity and waiting times are not stated.

resource.name: North West London Law Centres — Camden
resource.description: Free and independent legal advice and representation covering employment, housing, welfare benefits, asylum and immigration law.
resource.who: People living, working or studying in Camden who need help in one of the law centre's advice areas.
resource.access: Use the online contact form on the provider website to ask for help.
resource.check: Contact the law centre first to confirm that it can take your issue and whether funding or other eligibility criteria apply.
resource.coverage: People living, working or studying in Camden and Brent; this listing records the Camden service.

sources.note: The current provider page names the Camden and Brent catchment, advice subjects, free and independent service, and online contact route.
Camden Council's current advice network lists North West London Law Centres and confirms free advice on employment, housing, benefits, asylum and immigration.

candidates.evidence: The provider states that it offers free independent legal advice and representation to people living, working and studying in Camden and Brent, with an online contact form; Camden Council lists the same service and subjects.
candidates.limitations: The sources do not establish current capacity, waiting times, accessibility or the eligibility rules for each type of case. Contact the service before relying on help being available.

resource.name: Islington and Camden Young Carers service
resource.description: Individual, group and whole-family support for young carers, including advice, peer support and help reducing the impact of caring responsibilities.
resource.who: Young people under 18 who live in Camden and have caring responsibilities for a family member or friend.
resource.access: Call 0207 841 4445 or email icyc@childrenssociety.org.uk to ask for information or support.
resource.check: Contact the service to confirm its current assessment process, availability and the support it can offer.
resource.coverage: Young carers under 18 living in Camden or Islington; this listing records the Camden route.

sources.note: The current provider page states the under-18 Camden or Islington eligibility, support activities and direct phone and email access.
Camden Council describes young carers, names the service and publishes the same contact route.

candidates.evidence: The provider page says the service supports under-18s in Camden or Islington through tailored one-to-one work, groups, advice and whole-family support, and publishes direct phone and email access; Camden Council confirms the route.
candidates.limitations: Costs, current capacity, waiting times and detailed referral or consent arrangements were not stated. The listing does not extend the under-18 provider criteria to young adult carers.

resource.name: Citizens Advice Hillingdon
resource.description: Free, confidential advice and information on rights and practical problems, with general advice and specialist projects for more complex needs.
resource.who: Hillingdon residents seeking advice on matters such as benefits, debt, employment rights, housing, discrimination or other rights issues.
resource.access: Call the free Adviceline on 0808 278 7893, Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm, or use the provider's advice pages.
resource.check: Start with Adviceline so the service can assess whether general advice, a specialist project or another local provider is appropriate.

sources.note: The current provider home page confirms free confidential general advice, specialist projects, Hillingdon coverage and the freephone Adviceline.
The advice page lists rights topics, local access, specialist-project criteria and Adviceline hours.

candidates.evidence: Citizens Advice Hillingdon publishes a freephone borough-wide first contact for general advice, names benefits, debt and employment-rights support, and links rights topics including housing, discrimination, immigration and work.
candidates.limitations: Not every topic has local specialist casework, and eligibility for funded projects varies. The sources do not state current waiting times or guarantee an appointment.

resource.name: Hillingdon Domestic Abuse Advocacy Service
resource.description: Independent and confidential domestic-abuse advocacy, including telephone advice, risk assessment, safety planning and coordinated support.
resource.who: Adult victims aged 16 or over who live in Hillingdon, of any gender, and their children.
resource.access: Call 07874 620954 or email hdaas@hillingdon.gov.uk to ask for confidential help and advice.
resource.check: Use a safe device and contact method if possible. Ask the service to confirm its current response arrangements and the support available for your situation.
resource.coverage: Victims of domestic abuse living in Hillingdon

sources.note: The current council page states the borough and age criteria, all-gender and all-risk support, service activities and direct confidential contact route.
CNWL's current domestic-abuse page confirms the Hillingdon advocacy service and the same public phone contact.

candidates.evidence: Hillingdon Council says the service supports male and female Hillingdon victims at all risk levels, provides telephone advice, risk assessments and safety plans for clients aged 16 and over and their children, and publishes direct confidential contact details.
candidates.limitations: Current waiting times and capacity are not stated. The NHS page uses a slightly different service abbreviation and email address, so the listing uses the council service name and council contact route.
